correctness.rationale: In the Legendre equation write p(theta)=P_n(cos theta), integrate (sin(theta)p')'+n(n+1)sin(theta)p=0 against the exponential, and integrate sin(theta)p' by parts. This yields the stated weighted cos(theta) moment; elimination with the derivative identity gives the positive two-step recurrence, also at n=0 by E_1=a A_0. Two applications of the Legendre recurrence give the rational coefficient R_n. Its adjacent difference has the sign of F_z(n); Descartes' rule and F_z(1)>0 give the unique positive zero above 1. The transition equation is increasing in z and F_0 is negative for t≥2 (it is already negative at 2 and decreasing thereafter). The large-a zero is bracketed by t=a(c±ε), c=sqrt(7/3), using the opposite signs of (7−3c²)(c²+1). R_n>0 for n≥1, approaches 1 from above, and R_0 changes sign at z=3. Hence the finite coefficient constraints give the stated region, including ties and both endpoints. The tail is strictly positive in both parities for every admitted b since b>−1; the same parity check applies to the admitted pure oscillation. No numerical truncation is used for the universal assertions.
